description: Fan-out sweep at N = 1, 4, 8, 16, 28, 32. The slope matters more than any single point: it separates per-port cost from fixed overhead.
metric: sweep latency and per-port latency vs N
instrument: in-process timing across all three configs
notes: The most genuinely uncertain result in the suite, and the reason to run it early. In config B every HAL call marshals through json.dumps while holding the GIL (~7.6us measured), so all Python-touching threads serialise on it - a hard ceiling of roughly 130k HAL calls/sec regardless of thread count. Whether that inverts Rust's advantage under fan-out cannot be predicted, only measured.
